sourcesActuallyRead.organisation: Swiss Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office BLV
sourcesActuallyRead.readScope: Full core page, especially Grundlagen zur Krankheit and Symptome und Verlauf (web lines24–30). Infection follows ingestion of infected muscle tissue; infected animals can show no apparent symptoms. No regional legal or control procedure is reused.

Actual substantive paragraphs, web lines395–418, especially skeletal muscle, infectious muscle larvae as the transmitted stage and reproduction in intestinal mucosa. This contrasts the developmental locations; legal, measurement and clinical details are excluded.

sourcesActuallyRead.organisation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention CDC DPDx
sourcesActuallyRead.readScope: Causal Agents, Life Cycle and the adult-intestine/larva-muscle description, web lines25–45. Ingestion of muscle larvae; adult development in the small intestine; females release larvae that migrate to striated muscle. No species-wide encapsulation guarantee, measurements, times or diagnosis are taken.

Actual opening reference-laboratory text, web lines5–9: E.multilocularis adults in carnivore intestine, eggs in faeces, vole-type intermediate hosts ingest eggs and develop larval tissue, humans can be accidental intermediate hosts. Frost/time, treatment and law paragraphs are excluded.

sourcesActuallyRead.organisation: Medical University Vienna Institute for Specific Prophylaxis and Tropical Medicine
sourcesActuallyRead.readScope: Physical PDF page1, Lebenszyklus des Erregers and Übertragung read in original extraction and visually on local Poppler PNG. F.hepatica eggs hatch into a larva entering a snail intermediate host; development inside the snail precedes exit and encystment on vegetation as metacercariae; suitable definitive hosts ingest the latter. All sizes, durations, treatment and legal text are excluded.

questions.fourthChoice: Trichinelleneier, die mit verunreinigtem Futter aufgenommen werden
questions.whyPlausible: Tests confusion between a faecal–oral egg-transmission cycle and the taught muscle-larva route; it is distinct from the existing option that explicitly names fox tapeworm eggs.
questions.whyUnambiguouslyFalseHere: For the taught Trichinella transfer to a new host, the infectious material is muscle larvae in ingested tissue. Intestinal adult reproduction and new muscle larvae do not turn eggs in feed into that transmission route.
questions.claimLimit: Biological lifecycle comparison only; no claim that any particular food is safe or any required test can be omitted.

questions.fourthChoice: Ein möglicher Befall wäre dann auf den Darm begrenzt
questions.whyPlausible: Tests a compartment error, distinct from the existing blanket food-safety and skipped-test distractors.
questions.whyUnambiguouslyFalseHere: No apparent symptoms do not restrict the possible parasite lifecycle to the intestine. The independently described muscle-larva stage remains compatible with an outwardly unremarkable animal; the correct option still merely says infection is not excluded.
questions.claimLimit: No inference of an actual infection or its distribution in a particular animal; the invalid inference from appearance is rejected.

questions.fourthChoice: Fuchs und Nager sind beide Endwirte mit erwachsenen Würmern
questions.whyPlausible: Tests failure to distinguish the two host roles despite both animals carrying stages of the same parasite.
questions.whyUnambiguouslyFalseHere: The stated typical E.multilocularis cycle assigns the intestinal adult to the fox definitive host and larval stages to the rodent intermediate host, rather than adults in both.
questions.claimLimit: Typical named wild-animal cycle only; no assertion about all possible hosts, regional prevalence or individual diagnosis.

questions.fourthChoice: Eine an einer Pflanze haftende Metazerkarie
questions.whyPlausible: Transfers between the existing two parasite units: both involve oral acquisition, but the stage on vegetation belongs to the taught F.hepatica cycle rather than human E.multilocularis infection.
questions.whyUnambiguouslyFalseHere: FLI and UZH identify egg ingestion for human E.multilocularis infection. Independently, Medical University Vienna and CDC place vegetation-associated metacercariae in the Fasciola lifecycle, so this option cannot be a second correct fox-tapeworm stage.
questions.claimLimit: Cross-example lifecycle contrast only; no statement that vegetation in general carries a parasite or that a photograph determines contamination.

questions.fourthChoice: Sie ist ein Fehlzwischenwirt, in dem der beschriebene Zyklus endet
questions.whyPlausible: Transfers the accidental-host term from the existing tapeworm unit, while distinguishing it from a required, developmental intermediate host.
questions.whyUnambiguouslyFalseHere: Both sources describe active larval development in the suitable snail and subsequent departure toward the next stage. That snail is therefore an intermediate host in this cycle, not its described dead-end accidental host.
questions.claimLimit: Only the suitable intermediate snail in the displayed F.hepatica cycle; no assertion that every snail is suitable or infected.

questions.fourthChoice: Eine frisch aus dem Ei geschlüpfte Larve vor dem Befall der Schnecke
questions.whyPlausible: Distinguishes the early free larva before the snail from the existing distractor that remains inside the snail and from the later encysted metacercaria on vegetation.
questions.whyUnambiguouslyFalseHere: Both independent original descriptions place the newly hatched larva before entry into the snail. The suitable definitive host acquires the later metacercaria after the snail-associated development, not that early stage from vegetation.
questions.claimLimit: No measurements, swimming speed, dates, survival periods or cooking/freezing guidance; no clinical diagnosis or release decision.
